[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aihealthchat-59d2) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MumbaiHacks%202025%20--%20Round%201%20(Online)-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://mumbaihacks25-round1.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-5-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Your Shield Against Epidemics

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Natural language processing (NLP)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Natural%20language%20processing%20(NLP)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Twilio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Twilio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Whatsapp API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Whatsapp%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![langchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/langchain-333333?style=flat-square)

**Description of your solution**

SwasthAI is an **Autonomous Health Intelligence Agent Network** that demonstrates how AI agents can coordinate to provide proactive health monitoring and early epidemic detection. This hackathon prototype focuses on showcasing **true agentic behaviour** through autonomous decision-making, multi-agent coordination, and goal-oriented health surveillance workflows accessible via WhatsApp messaging.
The system transforms traditional reactive health reporting into a **proactive, agent-driven surveillance network** where specialized AI agents autonomously assess symptoms, detect patterns, coordinate responses, and escalate alerts without human intervention.


**Key Features**

- **Agentic Surveillance Orchestration:** A central coordinator manages specialized agents for symptom triage, pattern detection, and alerting, producing predictive insights and automated notifications from community-reported data.

- **WhatsApp Health Assistant:** Real-time symptom assessment over WhatsApp with adaptive, agent-driven dialogues and autonomous follow-up scheduling for check-ins and reminders.

- **Pattern Detection & Alerts:** Lightweight statistical anomaly detection flags unusual symptom spikes or clusters, triggering agent-led community alerts when thresholds are crossed.

- **Mock Government Interop:** Simulated connections to health databases via mock endpoints, demonstrating agent decisions for data sharing with basic consent and audit logging.

**Technical Implementation**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/04c6e710b19346088daf9375797857da/8f2d9e58-10d9-4d65-9695-dd972d28a59e.png)

1. **Multi-Agent Framework:** Orchestrate autonomous agents with a lightweight coordinator for triage, pattern analysis, communications, and alerting in a single end-to-end workflow.
 
2. **LLM Tooling:** Use function-calling to perform symptom triage, read/write database records, dispatch alerts, and trigger follow-ups directly from agent decisions.
 
3. **System Integration:** Handle real-time WhatsApp messaging via webhooks, route agent tasks through a FastAPI backend, and expose mock endpoints to simulate external health systems.
 
4. **Anomaly Detection:** Apply moving-window counts and simple thresholds to flag symptom/location spikes, emitting escalation signals that agents act on automatically.
 
5. **Scalable Architecture:** Start with a single-process app and a lightweight DB; roadmap includes cloud microservices, advanced forecasting models, high-throughput pipelines, hardened security, and real integrations.

**Specific Pain Points Addressed**

1. **Early Detection Through Automation**

 - **Autonomous Surveillance:** Agents continuously monitor without human oversight.
 - **24/7 Pattern Recognition:** Automated detection of symptom clusters and unusual health trends.
 - **Instant Escalation:** Agent-driven alerts eliminate human delay in critical situations.

2. **Coordinated Response Management**

 - **Multi-Agent Coordination:** Specialized agents handle different aspects of health surveillance.
 - **Automated Follow-ups:** Agents schedule and manage ongoing patient communications.
 - **Smart Resource Allocation:** Agents prioritize high-risk cases for immediate attention.

3. **Accessible Health Intelligence**

 - **WhatsApp Integration:** Leverages familiar messaging platform for broad accessibility.
 - **Autonomous Interviews:** Agents conduct structured health assessments independently.
 - **Proactive Outreach:** Agents initiate contact for follow-up care and community alerts.

**Target Audience**

1. **Primary Users:**

- Rural and semi-urban citizens (500M+ underserved)
- Community health workers (e.g., ASHA workers)
- State and district health departments
- National Health Mission (NHM) teams

2. **Secondary Users:**

- NGOs and public health organizations
- Research institutions and data analysts
- Corporates with employee health programs
- International health agencies (e.g., WHO, UNICEF)

**Go-to-Market Strategy**

- To Partner with state health departments for pilots integrated with frontline worker networks by aligning with National Health Mission and ABDM’s WhatsApp infrastructure. 
- Ensure DPDP compliance and clinical validation. 
- Collaborate with cloud providers and telemedicine platforms. 
- Promote at AI and healthcare forums for credibility and global partnerships.

**Revenue Model**

- **Per Alert Pricing:** Charges may range from ₹50 to ₹1,500 per health alert generated, scalable by volume and alert complexity.
- **Subscription Plans:** Tiered monthly subscriptions starting at ₹1 lakhs for supporting baseline alert volumes, with additional charges for exceeding thresholds.
- **Enterprise and Government Licensing:** Custom pricing for large-scale clients integrating alert systems into their infrastructure, enabling wide coverage and performance-based incentives.

**Healthtech: Bring your own problem in Healthtech, leveraging Agentic AI.**

SwasthAI tackles India's reactive public health crisis by creating an autonomous epidemic prevention network. It leverages a multi-agent AI system to transform 500 million rural and semi-urban citizens into a real-time disease surveillance grid, operating 24/7 via WhatsApp and SMS. This shifts the paradigm from delayed crisis management to proactive intervention. Specialized AI agents autonomously scan thousands of multilingual conversations to find anomalies, run predictive models to forecast outbreaks, and coordinate a data-driven response—all while learning and adapting. By integrating with national health infrastructure like ABDM, SwasthAI is a scalable, high-impact solution designed to detect and mitigate health crises before they escalate, embodying the future of agentic AI in public health.

> From Satellite Data to Actionable Insights.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vue.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vue.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Deep Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deep%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Problem Statement: Robust change detection, monitoring and Alert System on user defined Area of Interest using Multi-temporal Google Earth Engine satellite imagery

Solution: Gagan Dhrishti is a cloud-resilient change detection and alerting system built for monitoring user- defined Areas of Interest (AOIs) using multi-temporal Google Earth Engine’s satellite imagery.​

It leverages spectral analysis, machine learning, and temporal intelligence to differentiate between anthropogenic and natural changes, while overcoming challenges posed by cloud/shadow occlusion and seasonal noise.​

Gagan Dhrishti offers an end-to-end pipeline — from AOI selection to change classification, alerting, and GIS-compatible output delivery — all through a user-friendly web-based interface.​

Define the area of interest (AOI) for monitoring

Set thresholds, frequency, and type of changes to track

Apply algorithms to detect and quantify changes

Collect satellite imagery and preprocess it

Display results and send alerts

Monitoring based on user defined intervals
​
The major problem it solves is the problem of monitoring.

**Challenges we ran into**

During testing, AOI selection was smooth, but cloud cover in many satellite images caused degraded quality and loss of critical ground details, reducing change detection reliability.​

​Solution
Cloud Masking: We applied a cloud mask to each image, removing pixels affected by clouds and
shadows. ​

Temporal Compositing: To fill gaps, we created a temporal composite by taking the median of
images over time, yielding a seamless, cloud-free AOI mosaic.​

Result: The process effectively “sees through” clouds, ensuring high-quality, reliable imagery
for analysis.​

> Intellicruit: AI that reads resumes, scores candidates, and schedules interviews—so you hire the best, faster, while empowering HR teams and helping candidates shine.

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Whisper](https://img.shields.io/badge/Whisper-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Atlas](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Atlas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![transformer](https://img.shields.io/badge/transformer-333333?style=flat-square) ![Clerk](https://img.shields.io/badge/Clerk-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Recruitment is often time-consuming and manual, requiring HR teams to review hundreds of resumes and schedule interviews across different time zones.

Bias in candidate evaluation can lead to unfair hiring decisions and lack of diversity in the workplace.

Candidates struggle with inconsistent feedback, limited interview preparation resources, and unclear expectations for roles.

Existing systems are often fragmented, requiring multiple tools for resume parsing, scoring, scheduling, and feedback, leading to inefficiency.

Intellicruit solves these problems by:
Automatically parsing resumes (PDF, DOCX, images) to extract structured data like skills, experience, and certifications.

Scoring candidates objectively based on alignment with job descriptions, highlighting strengths and areas for improvement.

Providing instant feedback to candidates through AI-driven mock interviews, helping them prepare better.

Automating interview scheduling by matching HR and candidate availability, reducing manual coordination.

Offering AI-powered job recommendations based on resume analysis and market trends, helping candidates find better-fit opportunities.

Supporting continuous learning through course recommendations and certificate verification.

Reducing bias by focusing on skills, experience, and competencies rather than subjective factors.

Intellicruit streamlines the recruitment workflow for HR professionals and provides a fair, efficient, and data-driven experience for candidates.

Ultimately, Intellicruit helps organizations hire the right talent faster and empowers candidates to prepare effectively for technical roles.

**Challenges we ran into**

Parsing Diverse Resume Formats
Resumes came in various formats—PDF, DOCX, scanned images—which made it difficult to extract consistent data.
Solution: Integrated PyMuPDF and Unstructured (OCR) for parsing, with LangChain to unify context and structure across formats.

Ensuring Fair AI Scoring
Initial AI scoring models showed bias toward certain keywords and roles.
Solution: Refined prompt templates, used MCP (Model Context Protocol), and incorporated feedback loops to improve fairness and accuracy.

Synchronizing Multiple AI Agents
Coordinating Resume Agent, Scoring Agent, Mock Interview Agent, and Scheduler Agent led to data inconsistencies.
Solution: Implemented A2A (Agent-to-Agent) communication protocols and standardized data formats for smooth handoffs.

Mock Interview Timing & Realism
Managing question prompts, recording responses, and analyzing non-verbal cues in real-time was complex.
Solution: Combined pyttsx3 for TTS, OpenCV for video, Whisper for transcription, and custom silence detection for precise flow.

Scheduler Time Zone Handling
Parsing user-provided availability (like "Monday 2 PM") into real calendar dates across time zones was error-prone.
Solution: Used LLaMA3 for NLP parsing and built robust logic to map natural language times to actual time slots.

Managing API Limits & Performance
External APIs like Whisper and Groq (LLaMA3) often hit rate limits during bulk processing.
Solution: Added asynchronous task queues, batching, and retries to optimize API calls.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Werkzeug](https://img.shields.io/badge/Werkzeug-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The **Stampede Predictor** project tackles the critical issue of **enhancing public safety in crowded environments**. It aims to prevent dangerous situations by providing a proactive system for monitoring and analyzing crowd density and predicting potential stampede risks.

## Key Purposes

### Real-time Crowd Monitoring
Event organizers, security teams, and venue operators can utilize the live webcam feed analysis to get immediate visual feedback and risk status updates on crowd conditions as they happen.

### Analyzing Past Events
The ability to upload video and image files allows for detailed post-event analysis. This helps in understanding crowd behavior in specific areas, identifying bottlenecks or high-risk zones, and gathering data to improve planning for future events.

### Receiving Early Warnings
The system's core function is to detect escalating crowd density and indicate increasing risk levels (from Normal to CRITICAL RISK). This serves as a crucial early warning system, allowing personnel to intervene and manage the crowd before a dangerous situation develops.

### Informing Safety Planning
The insights gained from both live and file analysis can directly inform and improve existing crowd management strategies, security personnel deployment, and emergency response plans, making these tasks more efficient and safer.

### Data Integration
The real-time data stream published to Fluvio provides a valuable source of crowd metrics that can be consumed by other monitoring systems, data analytics platforms, or research tools, enabling more comprehensive safety infrastructures.

---

By offering these capabilities, **Stampede Predictor** transforms traditional, often reactive, crowd management into a more proactive, data-driven approach, significantly improving safety in densely populated public spaces.

**Challenges we ran into**

Here are some of the key challenges we encountered while building the Stampede Predictor and how we addressed them:

### Choosing a Suitable Detection Model
Initially, selecting the right AI model for person detection was a hurdle. We attempted to train a custom model, but this proved to be time-consuming, confusing, and ultimately unsuccessful within the hackathon timeframe.

### Iterating on Detection Models
After the custom model attempt, we explored pre-trained models. We first tried MobileNet SSD, but found that YOLO models offered better performance for our use case. This led us to pivot to the YOLO family.

### Selecting the Right YOLO Model
Within the YOLO family, there are various versions (v5, v8, v11) and sizes (nano, small, medium). We needed a model that balanced accuracy with inference speed for real-time analysis. After some testing, we chose YOLOv11 Nano ('yolo11n.pt') as it provided a good balance for our application's requirements.

### Setting Up Fluvio
Integrating Fluvio, the real-time data streaming platform, presented its own set of challenges. Getting the Fluvio cluster and topics configured correctly took some effort.

### WSL and Webcam Issues
Developing on Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) introduced complexities, particularly with webcam access and compatibility with OpenCV. Fluvio also did not have native support for Windows, requiring us to rely on WSL or consider Linux/macOS environments. We navigated these by focusing development and testing primarily within the recommended Linux/macOS environments and ensuring the code was compatible where possible.

### Various Other Bugs and Hurdles
As with any software development project, we ran into numerous smaller bugs and integration issues between different components (Flask, OpenCV, YOLO, Fluvio, and the frontend). These were typically resolved through careful debugging, consulting documentation, and iterative testing.

**InfinyOn/Fluvio Track**

The Stampede Predictor project powerfully demonstrates the capabilities of real-time data streaming by leveraging Fluvio as the central communication backbone for its crowd analysis. Rather than tightly coupling the computationally intensive video analysis directly with the web interface for display, we've designed the system to stream structured crowd density and risk data to a dedicated Fluvio topic, specifically 'crowd-data'. This architectural choice achieves significant **decoupling** between the backend AI processing and the frontend user experience.

This decoupling, enabled by Fluvio, brings crucial benefits: it enhances **scalability** because multiple consumers can independently read from the Fluvio stream without impacting the performance of the analysis service; it provides **flexibility** as new applications or services can easily subscribe to the 'crowd-data' topic to utilize the real-time insights; and it lays a robust foundation for **future integrations**, allowing the

> AI That Protects Before Accidents Happen.

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Computer Vision](https://img.shields.io/badge/Computer%20Vision-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Industrial environments like construction sites and factories face high safety risks, where workers are required to wear Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) such as helmets and safety vests. However, PPE compliance is typically monitored manually through supervisors or CCTV footage, which is inconsistent, labor-intensive, and often reactive.

As a result:

-Safety violations go unnoticed in real time
-Accidents occur due to delayed intervention
-There is no scalable way to monitor large workforces continuously

Our system addresses this by:

Continuously monitoring workers using AI-based computer vision
Detecting whether required PPE is being worn in real time
Instantly flagging violations and enabling proactive intervention
Reducing dependency on manual supervision
Improving overall workplace safety and compliance

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest hurdle was a class-mapping mismatch between training and app integration.
My dataset classes were correct in Roboflow, but different parts of the pipeline were expecting slightly different labels (for example no_gloves vs no-gloves) and sometimes relying on hardcoded class order. That caused wrong labels in predictions even when the model itself was performing well.

I also hit path issues because the dataset folder name had spaces, which broke some hardcoded training scripts.

How I solved it
I made the training flow read class names directly from data.yaml every time.
I removed hardcoded assumptions about class order and used the model’s exported names mapping.
I generated a class map artifact for integration so backend and frontend both consume the same source of truth.
I replaced brittle fixed paths with auto-detection of dataset root and YAML location.
I added quick validation/inference checks right after training to catch label mismatches immediately.
Outcome
After these fixes, the training pipeline became reproducible and integration-safe:
the same class IDs and names are now consistent across notebook training, backend inference, and frontend display.

### ReadyMe
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/readyme-f688) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/manyasharma1008/ReadyMe) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://ready-me-liart.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2mcOXZ4RGXw) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackNova%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknova-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> No more guessing your size.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Deep Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deep%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Keras CNN](https://img.shields.io/badge/Keras%20CNN-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Shopping for clothes online is frustrating because you never know if something will actually fit you. People usually guess their size or rely on confusing size charts that change from brand to brand.
Because of this, clothes often arrive too tight, too loose, or just don’t look good — leading to a lot of returns, wasted time, and disappointment.
Another big issue is that you can’t truly see how an outfit will look on your body before buying. You’re just imagining based on model photos, which are not realistic for everyone.

ReadyMe makes online shopping simple and more reliable.
Users can scan their body using their phone camera and get accurate measurements no manual measuring needed
It suggests the right size for each product, even if brands use different sizing systems
Users can see how clothes will actually look on them through virtual try-on (3D avatar or live camera)
This makes shopping:
Easier - no more guessing sizes
Faster - no trial and error
Safer - fewer wrong purchases and returns
In short, it helps people buy clothes that actually fit and look good the first time.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was building the 3D avatar from user images. It sounds simple in idea, but in reality it’s quite complex.
We struggled with how to accurately convert 2D images into a realistic 3D body model. Small issues like different camera angles, lighting, and user posture were affecting the output a lot. Even slight inconsistencies in images were leading to incorrect body shapes.
Another challenge was integrating this with real measurements. It’s not just about creating a visual avatar, but making sure it actually matches the user’s body dimensions so that virtual try-on makes sense.

To move forward, we broke the problem into smaller parts. Instead of building everything at once, we first focused on extracting body landmarks using tools like MediaPipe and generating approximate measurements. We are currently using this as a base and improving accuracy step by step.
For the 3D part, instead of jumping directly into full custom model building, we are exploring existing models and frameworks to understand how avatars are generated and then planning to refine them according to our use case.
Overall, the key was simplifying the problem, building step by step, and focusing on accuracy before realism.

**The problem it solves**

EquiMind - Zero Trust Risk Engine
GHR HACK 2.0 Submission

Problem Statement
Autonomous Zero-Trust Network Architecture with Dynamic Risk Scoring - Design a cybersecurity system implementing a Zero-Trust architecture where every user, device, and application is continuously verified using dynamic risk scoring instead of static authentication rules.

Solution Overview
EquiMind is a real-time zero-trust security platform that combines:

🤖 TensorFlow ML Models for threat prediction
📊 Real-time Risk Scoring with behavioral analysis
🔒 Dynamic Access Control based on continuous verification
💾 Supabase Database for dynamic entity management (20-person org)
📈 Prometheus Monitoring for observability
⚡ WebSocket Streaming for live security events

Risk Scoring Model
Risk scores (0-100) are computed from:

Network Analysis (33%): ML model prediction on network flow patterns
Identity Context (33%): MFA status, location, time-of-day
Device Posture (33%): Device health and compliance
Decision Thresholds:

0-40: ALLOW (Low risk)
40-65: CHALLENGE (Medium risk - require MFA)
65-80: RESTRICT (High risk - limited access)
80-100: BLOCK (Critical risk - deny access)

**The problem it solves**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/492594de513b4cb69a96d1c8f9b39476/6d87b413-f630-4c74-b32b-d91dec6f3d10.jpeg)

## Problem

Modern websites are built for manual human interaction. Users are expected to click buttons, fill forms, navigate complex interfaces, and repeat the same workflows every day.

While automation tools exist, they are often:
- too technical for everyday users  
- expensive to set up and maintain  
- fragile and prone to breaking  

Most people cannot realistically use tools like Selenium, RPA platforms, or custom scripts to automate their web tasks.

At the same time, AI systems such as chatbots can understand user intent, but they cannot see or control the real webpages users are working on. This creates a clear gap between what users want to do and what AI can actually execute on the web.

Today, there is no simple, safe, and universal way to tell an AI:
> “Do this for me on this website”

and have it happen directly on the live page the user is using.

---

## Solution

**Foxy AI** closes this gap by bringing intelligent, safe, and visual AI-driven automation directly into the browser.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Technical Approach and Challenges

We initially used **Playwright** for browser automation but faced multiple limitations. Playwright runs in a separate browser instance, which conflicted with our UCP requirement of operating in the **same live browser session**, similar to a browser extension. We also encountered access and control issues that made this approach unreliable for our use case.

Our early implementation relied solely on **DOM snapshots** provided as input to the AI. This proved problematic because:
- the DOM can change dynamically  
- popups and overlays often do not appear in the DOM  
- these issues frequently caused the agent to deadlock  

To address this, we switched to a **hybrid approach** using both:
- DOM snapshots  
- a **vision model** operating on page screenshots  

This allowed the agent to better understand the actual visual state of the page and make progress toward the user’s goal.

However, pure vision-based interaction was inaccurate for precise actions like clicking UI elements. To improve this, we introduced an **imaginary grid overlay** on the screenshot and mapped interactions to grid coordinates. This improved click accuracy by approximately **15%**.

Currently, we are using **free proxy vision models**, which have lower accuracy and higher latency compared to premium models. To resolve this, we have begun **fine-tuning our own model** to improve reliability and performance.

**AI Agent Security Track**

## Browser Automation Safety (Armoriq SDK + MCP)

We use **Armoriq’s SDK** with our **MCP server** to strictly control what our AI browser automation agent can do.

The agent operates on real user accounts, so all actions are **explicitly restricted and enforced at the system level**, not via prompts.

---

## How It Works

AI Agent → MCP Server → Armoriq SDK → Browser


- The agent proposes an action  
- MCP checks whether the action is allowed  
- Armoriq enforces execution rules  
- Only safe actions reach the browser  

The agent never executes actions directly.

---

## Permissions

**Allowed**
- Page navigation  
- Reading data (balances, holdings, history)  
- Fetching prices and market data  
- Screenshots and text extraction  

**Blocked**
- Buy/sell orders  
- Payments or withdrawals  
- Form submissions with side effects  
- Transaction confirmations or OTPs  

Anything not explicitly allowed is blocked by default.

---

## Result

- Financial and irreversible actions are impossible  
- Prompt injection and hallucinated actions are contained  
- Policies are immutable and enforced server-side  

This lets us safely use browser automation without risking user accounts or assets.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![FAST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/FAST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tauri](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tauri-333333?style=flat-square) ![langchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/langchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![Playwright](https://img.shields.io/badge/Playwright-333333?style=flat-square) ![FAISS](https://img.shields.io/badge/FAISS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Despite many essential services moving online, completing large and complex forms remains difficult for elderly users, students, and people who depend on assisted service centers. These workflows often involve long, multi-step forms, repeated data entry, document uploads, and strict validations, which are usually handled manually.

This manual process is time-consuming, error-prone, and frustrating for users and operators alike. Small mistakes can lead to rejections or delays, increasing dependency on intermediaries and limiting independent access to digital services. The core challenge is efficiently reusing existing user information and documents to accurately fill complex, form-heavy workflows.


jana-seva.ai is a guided, AI-assisted system that helps users complete complex online forms more efficiently while keeping them fully in control.

With user consent, the system organizes relevant personal information and documents (such as identity proofs and certificates) into a structured knowledge context. This allows the system to retrieve the exact data needed for specific form fields, significantly reducing repetitive manual data entry.

The system assists in filling safe and repetitive fields while leaving all authentication, verification, and submission steps entirely under user control. It also supports multiple user profiles, making it suitable for assisted service centers that handle applications for many individuals.

To improve accessibility for illiterate or less digitally confident users, the system can generate clear, step-by-step instructions and notifications (such as email or assisted prompts) to guide them through the process.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. **Understanding Messy and Inconsistent Government Forms**

One of the biggest challenges was scraping and understanding real-world government websites. These pages are not limited to clean input and label elements—many important fields are embedded inside tables, deeply nested layouts, or dynamically generated sections. In several cases, labels are not explicitly linked to inputs, and the actual meaning of a field is only visible visually on the page.

To overcome this, we moved beyond simple DOM selectors and started extracting additional contextual information such as nearby text, parent container content, and field ordering. In addition, we captured screenshots of the rendered page and mapped them with the scraped structural data to improve accuracy and validation. This combination of structural scraping and visual context helped us build a more reliable form-understanding layer instead of relying on brittle, hardcoded selectors.



2. **Supporting Multiple Users Safely**

Since assisted service centers often handle applications for many individuals, supporting multiple user profiles without data mixing was critical.

We addressed this by isolating user contexts and ensuring that all document data and form mappings are strictly scoped to the active profile.

**The problem it solves**

## 🌟 Overview

**DeepDive** is a comprehensive productivity platform that combines AI-powered webcam monitoring, gamification mechanics, and social features to help students stay focused during study sessions. Built with the MERN stack and powered by computer vision, it provides real-time feedback on concentration levels while making studying engaging through points, leaderboards, and clan competitions.

### 🎯 Problem It Solves

- **Distraction Management:** AI monitors your focus and alerts you when distracted
- **Procrastination:** Gamification and social pressure keep you motivated
- **Habit Building:** Streak tracking and daily goals build consistent study habits
- **Accountability:** Real-time monitoring and clan competitions provide social accountability

**Challenges we ran into**

# 🐛 Key Problems Encountered

### 1. **Authentication Token Error** 
Method `_generateTokens` had incorrect class binding - renamed to `generateTokens` and fixed `this` context. Blocked all user login/register attempts.

### 2. **WebSocket Connection Failures** 
Missing HMR config in `vite.config.js` caused constant WS errors. Added proper `host`, `strictPort`, and Socket.IO proxy settings.

### 3. **ML Vision API Cold Starts** 
Render.com free tier spin-up caused 5-8s delays. Implemented retry logic, reduced frame frequency to 3s, added loading UI.

### 4. **Incomplete Frontend Pages** 
Dashboard, Leaderboard, Clans, Settings were placeholders. Built fully functional pages with API integration (~1,500 lines).

### 5. **Redis Crashes** 
App crashed without Redis. Added `if (redisClient)` checks throughout for graceful degradation.

### 6. **Browser Extension Communication** 
Extension couldn't receive blocked site lists. Implemented Chrome runtime messaging API and event emitters.

### 7. **Token Refresh Race Conditions** 
Multiple concurrent token refreshes caused auth chaos. Added request queue with `_retry` flag.

### 8. **MongoDB Nested Updates** 
Partial setting updates overwrote entire objects. Used `$set` operator with dot notation.

### 9. **Negative Points Bug** (45 min)
Short sessions caused negative points. Added `Math.max(0, points)` guards and minimum duration checks.

### 10. **Webcam Permission Errors** (1 hour)
Denied permissions flooded console. Added try-catch blocks and permission UI with fallback mode.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![ngrok](https://img.shields.io/badge/ngrok-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Detecting and tracking critical objects in real-world environments is a major challenge — especially under conditions like low light, occlusion, fast motion, or varying camera angles. Traditional systems often fail to maintain accuracy, leading to safety risks, inefficiencies, or missed detections.

Object Vision AI addresses this challenge by combining real-time object detection with self-learning capabilities, ensuring continuous performance improvement without manual intervention.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into :-

Building Object Vision AI came with several real-world technical and deployment challenges. Each obstacle taught us something valuable about optimizing AI systems for real-time performance and scalability.

1. Camera Activation on Backend Startup
Problem:
Initially, the camera started automatically as soon as the Flask backend was launched — even before the frontend connected. This caused unnecessary resource usage and made it difficult to control the camera feed from the user interface.
Solution:
We modified the backend to initialize the camera only when a frontend request (button click) was received. This was achieved by restructuring the camera logic inside a route instead of the global scope. Now, users can start/stop the camera from the frontend dynamically.

2. CORS and Cross-Origin Communication Errors
Problem:
The frontend (running on a different port) couldn’t connect to the Flask backend due to CORS policy restrictions, blocking API requests and live streams.
Solution:
We integrated Flask-CORS and explicitly whitelisted our ngrok domain in the backend’s CSP (Content Security Policy). This allowed secure communication between the frontend, backend, and public ngrok URL without cross-origin conflicts.

3. Ngrok and URL Expiry Issues
Problem:
The ngrok public URL changed every time the backend restarted, breaking the frontend connection. Sometimes the tunnel also went offline.
Solution:
We configured ngrok with an authenticated reserved domain and automated reinitialization scripts to ensure the same endpoint stayed active during testing.

4. Model Latency During Real-Time Detection
Problem:
Running YOLOv8 in real time initially caused frame drops and high latency, especially on CPU.
Solution:
We optimized the inference pipeline by:
Reducing model size (switching to YOLOv8n)
Using threaded frame capture with OpenCV
Running inference asynchronously
This made detection smooth and stable even on moderate hardware.

5. Auto-Redeployment of Self-Trained Models
Problem:
After each retraining cycle, updating and redeploying the model across servers was manual and time-consuming.
Solution:
We implemented an automated redeployment pipeline that detects model updates, pushes the new weights to the backend, and reloads them without downtime.

6. Low-Light and Occlusion Challenges
Problem:
Objects under low illumination or partial visibility weren’t detected consistently.
Solution:
We extended the dataset with low-light augmentation techniques and applied contrast enhancement filters using OpenCV. After retraining, accuracy improved significantly under those conditions.

**Build Your Business with AI - Using Studio & Base44**

Base44 plays a crucial role in enhancing the connectivity, innovation, and scalability of Object Vision AI — allowing our system to go beyond just object detection and truly embody smart, cloud-connected vision.

1. Seamless API Integration :
We use the Base44 API to establish a smooth bridge between our frontend, backend, and external services.
It helps our AI system send and receive real-time detection data, manage API requests securely, and connect with the hosted YOLOv8 model through Base44’s scalable infrastructure.
This ensures that our detection pipeline remains fast, stable, and consistent across devices — no matter where the frontend or backend runs.

2. Cloud Connectivity & Deployment Support :
By integrating with Base44’s cloud environment, we deploy our Flask backend and AI model in a distributed setup.
This makes it possible to:
Stream live video frames from the frontend to the backend securely
Handle detection requests in real time
Access the public backend URL without hosting issues
This directly improves scalability and enables remote AI inference, so the user doesn’t need to run heavy models locally.

3. Real-Time Interaction Between Components : 
Base44 acts as a secure communication hub, allowing:
Frontend requests (like camera start/stop) to reach the backend instantly.
Processed detection results to be streamed back in real time.
API calls to remain stable even when using tools like ngrok or dynamic URLs

4. Innovation and Impact :
Base44’s infrastructure enabled us to focus on innovation rather than setup — letting us rapidly prototype and test features like:
Self-learning dataset expansion
Automated retraining and redeployment
Cloud-hosted vision inference

**The problem it solves**

🔍 The Challenge:
Credit card fraud is one of the most widespread financial crimes, costing the global economy over $40 billion annually.
Fraudsters exploit speed, scale, and system blind spots — performing thousands of transactions within milliseconds, often slipping past traditional rule-based systems.

Conventional fraud detection tools suffer from:
⚠️ Slow detection speed — can’t keep up with real-time transaction rates.
🧩 Low accuracy — high false positives cause inconvenience to legitimate users.
🔒 Lack of transparency — most ML models act as black boxes, leaving no explanation for decisions.
🧠 No behavioral context — they fail to analyze user habits, patterns, or anomalies dynamically.

🚀 The Solution :
The AI-Powered Credit Card & Transaction Fraud Detection System solves these challenges by introducing real-time, explainable, and intelligent fraud prevention.

It empowers banks, fintechs, and e-commerce platforms to:
🔐 Detect fraudulent transactions instantly using powerful ensemble machine learning models (XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest).
🧠 Understand why a transaction was flagged using Explainable AI (SHAP) insights.
⚡ Prevent losses proactively through automated risk scoring and instant alerts.
📊 Monitor trends visually via advanced Streamlit dashboards with live analytics and 3D risk visualization.
📧 Respond faster using email alerts for high-risk or critical transactions.

👥 How People Can Use It :
🏦 For Banks & Financial Institutions
- Integrate the system into transaction pipelines to flag suspicious activities in real time.
- Empower fraud analysts with visual explanations of risky transactions.
- Reduce manual review workload and financial loss due to fraudulent spending.

💳 For FinTech Startups :
- Quickly deploy a ready-to-use fraud detection SaaS for customers.
- Use the role-based access control to manage internal teams securely.

🔒 For Security Analysts :
- Access behavioral, temporal, and geographical insights to improve fraud prevention strategies.
- Leverage the risk scoring engine to prioritize investigations efficiently.

🌟 Why It’s Safer and Smarter :-
🧩 Explainable Decisions — Every flagged transaction comes with a clear reason using SHAP values.
⚙️ Automated Alerts — Immediate notifications reduce reaction time for fraud prevention.
🧮 Behavior-Aware AI — Learns user patterns to spot unusual spending or login behaviors.
🔐 Secure by Design — Passwords are encrypted with SHA-256, sessions are time-bound, and roles restrict data access.
🧭 Real-Time Intelligence — Dashboards and analytics update instantly to reflect system health, risk trends, and fraud metrics.

✅ In Simple Terms : 
This project makes online banking and transactions safer, faster, and more transparent.
It transforms traditional fraud detection from reactive and opaque into proactive, intelligent, and explainable — giving both users and institutions trust and control in every transaction.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building an AI-powered fraud detection system was both exciting and technically demanding. Several challenges emerged during development — from handling massive datasets to ensuring security and explainability.

⚙️ 1. Imbalanced Dataset Problem
Challenge:
The dataset had a severe class imbalance — fraudulent transactions made up less than 1% of total records. This caused most models to overfit towards “non-fraud” predictions, lowering recall for actual fraud cases.

Solution:
I used SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) to balance the dataset.
This significantly improved the model’s ability to detect minority (fraud) cases without compromising overall accuracy.

🧠 2. Balancing Accuracy with Explainability
Challenge:
Ensemble models like XGBoost and LightGBM achieved high accuracy but acted as black boxes, making it hard to explain why a transaction was flagged as fraud.

Solution:
I integrated SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) to visualize feature contributions for each prediction.
This added transparency and helped analysts understand “why” behind every alert.

📧 3. Email Alert Configuration
Challenge:
Implementing real-time email alerts using Gmail SMTP faced multiple issues — SSL configuration errors and “less secure app” restrictions caused email delivery failures.

Solution:
I resolved this by using Yagmail with app-specific passwords and SSL encryption (port 465), ensuring secure and reliable email notifications.

🧩 4. Session and Role Management in Streamlit
Challenge:
Streamlit’s default session handling doesn’t support multi-user role-based systems easily.
Creating persistent login states for Admin, Manager, and User roles caused repeated authentication resets.

Solution:
I used st.session_state variables to maintain user sessions, login timestamps, and lockout policies.
This enabled proper role-based access control and automatic session timeout after inactivity.

💾 5. Large Data Processing & Latency
Challenge:
Processing over a million transactions in real time caused performance lags during visualization and prediction.

Solution:
I optimized the workflow by:
- Using Pandas vectorization instead of loops.
- Implementing model caching with @st.cache_resource to prevent reloading models repeatedly.
- Compressing datasets and precomputing key metrics.

These optimizations reduced dashboard latency and made predictions nearly instantaneous.

🔒 6. Secure Credential Management
Challenge:
Storing email passwords and API keys inside the code was unsafe and against best practices.

Solution:
I shifted all credentials to Streamlit’s secrets.toml and .env files, ensuring sensitive data stayed encrypted and outside version control.

✅ Outcome :
Every challenge pushed me to learn practical ML engineering, security compliance, and real-time system design.

**Cybercrime Detection & Prevention**

The AI-Powered Credit Card & Transaction Fraud Detection System directly addresses one of the most critical forms of cybercrime — financial fraud in digital transactions.
In today’s digital economy, cybercriminals exploit loopholes in banking systems to perform unauthorized transactions, identity theft, and impersonation attacks.

This project acts as an AI-driven defense mechanism that detects and prevents such fraud in real time.

🧠 How It Detects Cybercrime :
1. Machine Learning-Based Anomaly Detection

- Uses advanced ML models (XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest) to identify unusual spending behaviors, login times, or transaction patterns that deviate from normal user behavior.
- These anomalies often indicate stolen credentials or card misuse, a common cybercrime tactic.

2. Behavioral & Velocity Analysis

- The system tracks transaction frequency, amount velocity, and geolocation distance.
- Sudden high-value transactions or rapid purchases from different locations trigger real-time alerts — helping stop bot-driven fraud and account takeovers.

3. Explainable AI (SHAP)

- Unlike black-box models, this system explains why a transaction is considered risky.
- This transparency improves trust and helps cybersecurity analysts investigate incidents faster.

4. Real-Time Risk Scoring

- Each transaction is evaluated and labeled from MINIMAL → CRITICAL risk.
- The system can automatically block, flag, or alert on high-risk events, preventing cybercrimes before financial loss occurs.

5. Email Alert System

- Sends encrypted notifications to users and administrators when suspicious activity is detected.
- This ensures immediate response to ongoing cyberattacks.

🧩 How It Prevents Cybercrime

- Implements SHA-256 encryption for passwords and secure logins.
- Enforces role-based access control to prevent unauthorized data access.
- Integrates multi-layer decision logic to validate both user identity and transaction behavior.
- Provides real-time dashboards for continuous monitoring of threats, system health, and alerts.

👉 Together, these features form a cyber defense framework capable of detecting, analyzing, and preventing digital financial crimes.

**Description of your solution**

**Problem Statement**
Across India, millions of students preparing for exams like JEE, NEET, UPSC, and board exams are trapped in a cycle of misinformation. In Telegram groups, WhatsApp forwards, and viral YouTube shorts, misleading study hacks, fake exam circulars, and leaked paper rumors spread faster than official updates. This culture of quick fixes not only fuels confusion but also severely impacts student's confidence, strategy, and mental health leading to wasted efforts, misplaced hope, and rising exam anxiety. Students desperately want clarity and trusted guidance but are overwhelmed by a flood of unchecked, viral content that sounds smart but is often false or misleading.

**Our Solution: Padhai Check — Agentic AI Study Companion**
Padhai Check is an innovative AI-powered platform designed specifically to fight exam-related misinformation and stress among students. It’s more than a fact-checker it’s a proactive, empathetic learning companion that understands the unique challenges students face in a fast-paced, digital ecosystem.
**Conversational, Code-Mixed Language Support:** Communicates naturally in Hinglish, the way students actually speak and share information.
**Multi-format Input:** Verifies text, screenshots, photos, and PDFs of viral exam hacks, fake circulars plus direct chat-based verification.
**Trusted Source Verification:** Cross-checks claims against verified official resources—NCERT textbooks, NTA circulars, UGC notifications, and exam board advisories.
**Clear Verdicts & Simple Explanations:** Provides easy-to-understand, bilingual feedback so students can quickly trust and act on information.
**Trend Monitoring Dashboard:** Tracks and exposes emerging misinformation trends in real-time, enabling students, parents, and educators to stay informed and vigilant.
**Emotional Wellbeing Support:** Incorporates a wellbeing companion that detects stress in queries and offers motivational nudges and stress relief tips.
**Personalized Alerts:** Sends custom notifications based on the student’s exam track (JEE, NEET, UPSC, Boards) alerting them instantly to official updates.

**Why It Matters**
Exam misinformation isn’t just an annoyance it directly harms student's academic outcomes and mental health. Students lose precious time chasing shortcuts that don’t work and spiral into anxiety that undermines their potential. Padhai Check empowers students to confidently separate fact from fiction, adopt effective study strategies, and maintain emotional balance.

**Target Audience & Impact**
Primary: Students aged 15–25 preparing for competitive and board exams—those most vulnerable to viral misinformation.
Secondary: Parents, educators, EdTech platforms, and policymakers who need actionable insights and tools to protect and support students.

**Go-to-Market Strategy**
Padhai Check will be launched as a free student dashboard to provide instant and inclusive access for exam aspirants across India. The initial focus will be on awareness and adoption, driven through strategic partnerships with coaching institutes, student influencers, and campus campaigns under the theme “Verify Before You Believe.” 
India’s USD 2.8 billion EdTech sector (2024) is projected to reach USD 33.2 billion by 2033 (CAGR 28%), with test prep growing to USD 9 billion by 2030. With over 2.4 million JEE and NEET aspirants and recent incidents of 120+ fake exam-related accounts flagged by NTA, there’s a clear need for a trusted verification system like Padhai Check. In the future, Padhai Check will evolve beyond a student tool into a trusted verification layer for the entire EdTech ecosystem. Other learning apps and institutions will be able to plug into our system to instantly verify exam-related information, ensuring accuracy and reliability across platforms just like how UPI became the common backbone for digital payments in India.
Our revenue model will be built around institutional subscriptions, strategic partnerships with EdTech and mental health organizations, and sponsored wellbeing initiatives. In the long term, Padhai Check aims to evolve into India’s trusted academic verification standard, with regional language expansion and integration with government education portals to maximize reach and impact aligning with India’s projected USD 10.4 billion EdTech opportunity by 2025.

Padhai Check is more than a tech solution — it’s a movement to rebuild trust, clarity, and calm in India’s high-pressure exam culture. It empowers students to focus on learning, not rumors. In a world where misinformation spreads faster than truth, Padhai Check becomes the student’s reliable companion — one that listens, verifies, and guides. Our vision is to develop **Impact-first AI solution** that makes truth as viral as fear, ensuring that every learner in India studies with confidence, credibility, and peace of mind.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/3770dd85886146b9be6fd9b1764223b3/2a0915d5-c36d-404e-989b-7029028a48fe.png)

**Misinformation: Bring your own problem in Misinformation, leveraging Agentic AI.**

Our project, Padhai Check, is a direct fit for the Misinformation track, tackling a high-stakes problem: the flood of fake exam circulars, paper leak rumors, and shortcut “study hacks” that dominate WhatsApp, Telegram, and YouTube. For exam aspirants, this misinformation is not harmless chatter — it drives poor preparation strategies, misplaced confidence, and severe exam anxiety.

At its core, Padhai Check is an antidote to this ecosystem. Its primary function is to verify and debunk viral academic claims, grounding answers in verified sources like NCERT, NTA circulars, UGC notices, and official exam boards. Students can paste text, upload screenshots, or share suspicious circulars, and instantly receive a clear verdict — True, Fake, or Misleading.

We leverage Agentic AI to move beyond passive fact-checking. Our intelligent study companion:
1. Proactively monitors student networks and issues real-time alerts on fake circulars and viral hacks.
2. Acts on behalf of students by sending personalized notifications for their exam track (JEE, NEET, UPSC, Boards), including instant debunks and official updates.
3. Shields wellbeing by detecting panic signals and nudging students with stress-busting tips.

Instead of forcing students to navigate a maze of rumors, Padhai Check becomes their trusted ally — verifying the viral, surfacing the official, and protecting both their preparation and peace of mind.

> “AI Bridge for Ayurvedic & Modern Diseases”

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Natural language processing (NLP)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Natural%20language%20processing%20(NLP)-333333?style=flat-square) ![langchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/langchain-333333?style=flat-square)

**Description of your solution**

**Project Name**: AYUSHAgent

**Problem Statement:**

AYUSH refers to traditional Indian systems of medicine, including Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy. These clinics use traditional terms (like Madhumeha for Diabetes), while modern hospitals and insurance systems rely on standardized ICD-11 (WHO) codes (like 5A11). This mismatch leads to fragmented patient records, **rejected insurance claims, and incomplete data for doctors and government health systems**.

Additionally, if a patient transitions from AYUSH treatment to modern medicine, the modern doctor may not have access to the patient’s previous AYUSH records. In such cases, the doctor may start treatment from scratch (a “0-level” approach), which can result in **delayed care, redundant tests, and increased treatment costs.**

AYUSHAgent bridges this gap by making AYUSH diagnoses compatible with modern **EMRs, insurance systems, and national health databases, ensuring continuity of care** and cost-effective treatment.

**Overview** : 
An bridge between Ayurvedic Disease and Modern Disease.
AI-powered system that connects India’s AYUSH/NAMASTE diagnoses with ICD-11(WHO) codes used in modern medicine

**Detail view :**
**AYUSH** = Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy. It’s India’s traditional medicine system.

**NAMASTE portal** = The Indian government’s digital system to record AYUSH patient data.
It stores disease names, treatments, and diagnoses in traditional medicine terms.

**ICD-11** = International Classification of Diseases, version 11, by WHO.
Used worldwide in hospitals, insurance, and EMR systems to standardize disease names. Every disease has a unique code.

**Agentic AI Implementation (How it works):**

1. The project uses **multiple AI agents** working together to solve a real healthcare problem:

2. **Extraction Agent:** Reads and understands traditional AYUSH terms.

3. **Mapping Agent:** Finds accurate ICD-11 equivalents.

4. **Validation Agent:** Ensures the mapping is correct and generates confidence scores.

5. **Output Agent:** Prepares structured, FHIR-compliant data for EMRs and insurance systems.

**What makes it different from ChatGPT or Google:**

*1. 100% aligned with India’s EHR 2016, ABDM, and Ayush Grid.
2. Ensures interoperability.
3. Uses official standards (NAMASTE + ICD-11).
4. Full EMR, insurance, and analytics-ready integration.
5. Supports Ayushman Bharat Card and IRDA insurance claim systems.*

**Example & Problem:**

A patient visits an Ayurveda clinic and is diagnosed with **Madhumeha (Ayurveda term for Diabetes).**
Modern hospitals, however, record Diabetes as **ICD-11(WHO) code 5A11.**

**Problem:**

1. AYUSH records and modern hospital records don’t match.
2. Insurance claims can be rejected.
3. Patient history is incomplete.
4. No data sharing between AYUSH and hospitals.

**How AYUSHAgent Fixes It:**

1.  Extraction Agent reads and understands the AYUSH diagnosis (Madhumeha). 
2.  Mapping Agent finds the correct ICD-11 code (5A11). 
3.  Validation Agent checks the mapping and provides a confidence score.
4.   Output Agent generates FHIR-compliant data that EMRs, insurance systems, and national health databases can use.

**Result:**

1. Insurance claims are accepted.
2. Government database has entry of clear details.
3. Patient records are complete and interoperable.
4. Data is usable for analytics, research, and government reporting.

**Healthtech: Bring your own problem in Healthtech, leveraging Agentic AI.**

Our project AYUSHAgent bridges India’s traditional AYUSH systems and modern digital health records, enabling seamless interoperability between clinics, hospitals, and insurance platforms.
Using Agentic AI, it intelligently maps traditional diagnoses to ICD-11 codes, making data clinically usable and globally standard.
Aligned with EHR 2016, ABDM, and Ayush Grid, it advances India’s move toward integrated, AI-driven healthcare.

**Description of your solution**

💡What We Plan to Build

We’re building ThinkBrowser, an AI-powered browser / browser extension that acts as a real-time fact companion.
Whenever a user visits an article, post, video, or thread — ThinkBrowser activates a “Critical View” mode, which:

Detects claims, opinions, and emotionally charged statements using NLP.

Provides context cards with verified sources, counter-arguments, and alternative perspectives.

Includes a “View vs. Counterview” toggle that displays balanced information rather than labeling something as “fake.”

Adds an AI truth meter showing how verifiable or speculative a statement is.

Gives a Critical Thinking Score to help users reflect before sharing or believing.

This is not about telling users what to believe — it’s about helping them see all sides clearly and decide for themselves.

🚨 Pain Points It Addresses

Misinformation Overload: People are constantly bombarded with fake or biased information and lack time to verify everything.

Echo Chambers: Algorithms often reinforce users’ existing beliefs.

Lack of Context: Users see isolated claims without understanding the full story or data.

Critical Thinking Gap: Most tools “flag” content instead of teaching people how to think critically.

Low Trust in Fact-Checkers: Labeling something as “false” often causes backlash and polarization — this tool provides facts, not verdicts.

🎯 Target Audience

Students & Educators: To promote media literacy and academic integrity.

Professionals & Journalists: Who need verified info quickly without bias.

Everyday Internet Users: Anyone scrolling news, Reddit, or Twitter (X) who wants to avoid being manipulated.

Policy & NGO Workers: For research and debunking misinformation campaigns.

🚀 Go-To-Market Strategy (GTM)

Phase 1: Early Adopters

Launch as a browser extension (Chrome, Brave, Edge) with a waitlist and demo.

Partner with media literacy orgs and universities to pilot test it in classrooms.

Viral growth through social media examples (“AI shows me both sides in 5 seconds”).

Phase 2: Expansion

Integrate into news platforms and search engines as a plug-in API.

Collaborate with AI newsletters / journalists / fact-checkers for content partnerships.

Add mobile companion app with “link analysis” feature (paste link → get all verified viewpoints).

Phase 3: Global Rollout

Launch in regional languages (Hindi, Tamil, Bengali, etc.).

Partner with local news channels and universities for credibility.

Freemium Model:

Free tier: Basic fact/context checks.

Premium: Advanced critical scores, academic citation mode, real-time media summaries.

API Integration: Sell “truth-layer API” to publishers and edtech platforms.

Institutional Licensing: Subscription for universities, NGOs, and governments to deploy internally.

B2B Partnerships: Integrate with productivity tools like Notion, Slack, or news dashboards.

Ad-Free Premium Tier: Optional subscription for clean UX and extra insights.

Perspective generation (GPT-4/5 fine-tuned model for neutral tone)

**The problem it solves**

# ForensIQally: Revolutionizing Digital Forensics with AI 
📑 [View Presentation Deck](https://www.canva.com/design/DAGqbzddEp0/lutjjeCo01JNnMyAmxFe-w/view?utm_content=DAGqbzddEp0&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=h677efcba7d)  
> **📢 TIP:** Please watch the demo for detailed explanation.

Note: The code for the landing page is in github and the rest on Huggingface.

## The Problem It Solves  
The digital forensics industry is struggling with three major challenges:  
- Over **3.5 million unfilled cybersecurity positions globally**.  
- **Cyberattacks increasing by 38% every year**.  
- The **average time to detect a breach is still 287 days**.  

Existing tools aren’t enough:  
- **SIEM platforms** like Splunk and QRadar are expensive, difficult to set up, and require months of specialized training.  
- **Forensic suites** like EnCase and FTK cost between $3K and $15K per license, and they have steep learning curves.  
- **Open-source tools** such as Autopsy and Volatility require deep technical expertise and involve too many manual steps.  
- **Cloud-based solutions** like AWS Detective or Azure Sentinel lock users into vendors, limit customization, and add ongoing subscription costs.  

The result? Organizations are drowning in endless log files while attackers continue to move freely through their systems.  

---

## How ForensIQally Makes Tasks Easier and Safer  
ForensIQally is designed to simplify digital investigations and make them accessible to teams that don’t have enterprise-level budgets or expertise.  
### Faster Incident Response  
With traditional tools, analyzing logs can take 8–12 hours. ForensIQally delivers a complete incident narrative, a detailed timeline, and remediation steps in under 30 minutes. That’s more than a 90% reduction in time.  
### Affordable and Accessible  
Instead of paying thousands of dollars for licensing, users can start with a **freemium model** that includes one free upload, with premium features at a fraction of traditional costs.  
It’s built for SMEs, small security teams, junior analysts, IT staff, and even students.  
### Smarter AI-Driven Analysis  
ForensIQally Core uses **Llama 3.3 70B** with seven specialized AI endpoints for investigation tasks. It supports multiple log formats, from Windows Event Logs to compressed archives, and automatically links findings to the **MITRE ATT&CK framework**, explaining attack patterns in plain English.  
### Education and Skill Building  
ForensIQally is the only forensic tool that doubles as a learning ecosystem:  
- **ForensIQwiz** gamifies cybersecurity learning with XP and collectible pets.  
- **Query Foxy** turns AI conversations into flashcards for quick revision.  
- A **6-module certification course** helps users gain official credentials.  
- A **case study library** presents real-world incidents through AI-generated narrations.  
### ForensIQshell 
- CLI tool inspired by shellgpt, but FREE! 
- Cross-Platform(Generates commands for Windows (CMD/PowerShell), Linux, and macOS), Rag Enhanced & Ethical
### Privacy-First Design  
All investigations are processed in real-time with **automatic PII redaction**. No logs are stored, ensuring complete privacy and data protection.  

---

## Why It’s Different  
- **Speed**: Investigations that take hours manually can be completed in minutes.  
- **Cost**: Traditional forensic suites cost thousands per license, while ForensIQally is accessible to anyone.  
- **Intelligence**: Instead of just parsing logs, it provides clear explanations, attack mapping, and suggested remediation.  
- **Education**: Built-in gamified learning and certification make it easier to close the cybersecurity skills gap.  
- **Privacy**: Zero retention ensures sensitive data never leaves your control.  

---

## Technology Behind the Platform  
The power of ForensIQally comes from its technical foundation:  
- A **multi-format log parser** that automatically detects and processes everything from JSON and TXT to Windows EVTX and Linux systemd journals.  
- Specialized **AI endpoints** optimized for root cause analysis, impact assessment, timeline generation, and remediation planning.  
- A **retrieval-augmented generation system** connected to Pinecone and the complete MITRE ATT&CK framework, enabling semantic search through millions of attack techniques.  
- A **cloud-native architecture** built with Python, Streamlit, and Firebase for scalability, reliability, and secure handling of sensitive forensic workloads.  

---

## In Summary  
ForensIQally is:  
- **Faster** → Hours reduced to minutes.  
- **Cheaper** → A fraction of enterprise forensic costs.  
- **Smarter** → Context-driven insights with MITRE ATT&CK built-in.  
- **Educational** → A complete ecosystem for learning and certification.  
- **Safer** → Privacy-first, with no data retention.  
It’s not just a tool—it’s the **future of digital forensics and cybersecurity education**.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into  

While building ForensIQally, I faced several technical hurdles that pushed me to adapt and improve both my code and approach.  

## Formatting LLM Outputs  
The biggest challenge was getting the LLM output to match the exact format I needed.  
- I built custom **output parsers** to generate sections, charts, and visuals.  
- The model often gave inconsistent structures, so I had to **enhance the parsers** across all apps to make them more robust.  

## Deployment on Hugging Face  
Running locally vs. deploying on Hugging Face came with its own problems:  
- Some packages I used on my local environment weren’t supported on Hugging Face.  
- There were **version mismatches** because my local setup was more updated than HF’s environment.  
- I had to **redesign parts of the UI** to fit the package versions available on Hugging Face.  

## ElevenLabs Podcast Generation  
Creating the podcast narrations with ElevenLabs was tricky:  
- Getting it to use **SSML** (speech markup) for natural, expressive voices was difficult.  
- I had to retry many times, worried my credits would run out before I produced something good.  

## Data Caching and Self-Coded Apps  
I coded all apps myself (except for using Windsurf for the landing page and some debugging due to time constraints).  
- Caching data and making it reusable across apps was challenging.  
- For **ForensIQshell**, the hard part was detecting the OS and shell type reliably.  

## Building ForensIQwiz  
ForensIQwiz was fun to build but came with its own hurdles:  
- Issues with **displaying and updating the leaderboard**.  
- Problems letting users **unlock pets with XP**.  
- Debugging the gamification logic took more time than expected.  

## Building Query Foxy  
Query Foxy’s main chat logic was straightforward since I had prior experience with chatbots. The bigger challenges were:  
- **Persisting chat history** across sessions.  
- Enabling **exports** as PDF summaries.  
- Building **interactive gamified flashcards** from conversations.  

---

In the end, the main takeaway was this: every time the LLM output didn’t fit my design, I improved my parsers. That mindset helped me overcome most of the blockers across all apps.

**All Registered Participants**

# Landing Page and WIndsurf Integration  

As mentioned, **all the main ForensIQally services were self-coded**. However, I leveraged **Windsurf** to build and enhance the **landing page**, which serves as the central hub for accessing all features.  

## Key Points  

- The landing page was developed using **HTML, CSS, and JavaScript**.  
- It acts as the **go-to hub** for students and users to access all ForensIQally functionalities.  
- Windsurf was also used to **fix minor bugs** and improve the overall user experience.  

This approach allowed me to focus on building the **core apps and AI-powered services** while providing a polished and functional interface for users.

**Voice AI & Conversational Products | Powered by Elevenlabs**

# Student Support with Case Studies  

ForensIQally includes a **student-focused support feature** called **Case Studies**, designed to help learners practice real-world digital forensics.  

## How It Works  
- Students can **run sample logs** through ForensIQally and generate a **full analysis**.  
- Each log comes with an **audio podcast narration** that:  
  - Explains the analysis clearly.  
  - Presents it like a **cybercrime story**, making learning engaging and immersive.  

## Podcast Integration  
- The podcasts are created using **ElevenLabs**, which allows for:  
  - **Natural, expressive speech** using SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language).  
  - A storytelling style that makes each case feel like a real **Cybercrime 101 episode**.  

This feature turns standard log analysis into a **hands-on learning experience**, helping students understand both the technical and narrative aspects of cybersecurity incidents.
